notes: High-performance game studio building live NPC personalization + in-game chat moderation. CTO (Rana) is very latency-focused: "sub-50ms 95th tail for short chat calls". Cost is a big factor - 24/7 inference for global player base. Interested in batching/caching to reduce cost but cannot increase tail latency. Wants deterministic routing: EU players -> EU, fallback to smaller quantized model when capacity saturated. Security: must support SSO/SAML, customer-managed KMS, and per-request audit logs. Quoted: 'We will tolerate small accuracy hit for 4x cost reduction but not >8% drop in conversational quality.'

workload_summary: Primary workload: short-turn conversational requests (~8-40 tokens per reply) for 500k MAU, peak concurrency ~6k rps in bursts. Targets: p95 latency <50ms for chat, avg token cost target < $0.0006/token. Model preference: small-medium open models (13B quantized), ability to fallback to 7B quantized. Requires prefix/KV caching for repeat contexts and routing by region. Wants Redwood Optimize recommendations on batching thresholds and quantization profiles.
poc_scope: 2-week technical POC: 1) baseline latency/cost for hosted API 13B FP16, 2) quantized 8-bit model run to measure quality vs cost, 3) evaluate continuous batching under burst load, 4) test prefix/KV caching with 30-day cache TTL, 5) region routing + failover. Deliverables: perf report (p50/p95/p99), cost per 1M tokens, quality regression delta on 3 conversational testsets.
perf_benchmark_requests: steady-state 1k rps for 2 hours - measure p50/p95/p99 and token throughput
burst test: ramp 0->6k rps in 30s - measure tail latency and failed requests
quantization A/B: 13B FP16 vs 13B 8-bit and 7B 4-bit - run identical prompt set and CR metrics
batching sweep: evaluate batching sizes 1,2,4,8 with target latency SLOs
cache effectiveness: simulate 30% prefix reuse and measure token savings
